# Instructions for accurately reporting failed municipal water-quality tests to protect the public

1. Start with the inspection records.

completion:
Identify any instances where samples failed to meet the prescribed standards.
3. Document the specific parameters that failed, such as chlorine residue, E. coli levels, turbidity, pH levels, etc.
4. Use standard reporting formats for water-quality reports, ensuring all required data fields are completed accurately.
5. Clearly state the sampling date and location.
6. Detail the specific violations or deviations from standards.
7. Include the test results and compare them to the safe limits set by relevant authorities, such as the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) or local health departments.
8. Describe any immediate remedial actions that were taken, like increasing chlorine levels, flushing the system, or issuing boil water advisories.
9. Outline ongoing actions or corrective measures planned to address the root causes of the failures.
10. Report any notifications sent to the public or health officials regarding the failed tests.
11. Discuss if there were any potential health risks associated with the failed tests and
